transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on things the way I used to. At work, I’ll be looking at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list and realize I’ve read the same line over and over. Then I put off making calls because even simple decisions feel harder than they should.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yes. Most days I feel this kind of dull heaviness, like it’s just sitting with me. Even when I’m doing things that used to help—going to the community center or working in my garden—I’m there, but I don’t really feel lifted by it. I feel like I’m just going through the motions, putting on a smile.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been a little over two years now. It started after my close friend died, and I just… never really felt like I came back from it.
Have you experienced any periods where your sadness feels much worse than it does on average?

It’s not so much sharp ups and downs. Most days it’s just this steady dull heaviness. I can be at the community center or out in my garden, places that used to make me feel better, and I’m still just kind of going through the motions with a smile on my face.
Do you have difficulty experiencing pleasure most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, I do. Most days it feels like there’s this dull heaviness with me, and even when I’m doing things I used to enjoy, like going to the community center or working in my garden, I don’t really feel much pleasure from it. I’m there, but it’s like I’m just going through the motions with a smile on.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or that can lift your mood, even if it's just a little bit?

Not really, no. I still go to the community center, and I still spend time in my garden because I know those things used to help me. But most days there’s just this dull heaviness there with me, and I feel like I’m doing the motions more than actually enjoying it. Maybe it takes the edge off a little sometimes, but it doesn’t really lift me the way it used to.
Would you say your symptoms are interfering with your daily life and relationships in a significant way?

Yes, I’d say it is. At work, I’ve started putting off client follow-ups at the credit office, which isn’t like me. And outside of work, I’ve pulled back from things I used to make a point of doing, like gallery events and walking-club outings. I’m still managing, but it’s definitely affecting my day-to-day life.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain since you started feeling this way?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed any big change in my weight one way or the other. My clothes seem to fit about the same, so I don’t think there’s been anything significant.
Would you describe your current state as feeling persistently sad or depressed for most of the day?

Yes. Most days I do feel down, kind of like there’s a dull heaviness sitting with me. Even when I’m at the community center or out in my garden, I’m usually just going through the motions, maybe putting on a smile, but I don’t really feel lifted.
Have you had two or more years of continuous depressive symptoms?
Yes. It started after my close friend died, a little over two years ago, and it’s been there pretty much since then.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Not really, no. I still go to the community center and I still spend time in my garden, but they don’t lift me up the way they used to. Most days it feels like I’m just going through the motions, maybe smiling because I’m supposed to, but I don’t really feel much pleasure in it.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. The community center and my garden used to make me feel better, but now most days I’m just there, doing the motions. I might smile, but it feels kind of pasted on. There’s this dull heaviness that doesn’t really lift.
Do you feel like you've lost interest or pleasure in almost all activities most of the time?

Yes, most of the time. There’s just this dull heaviness with me most days. Even when I’m at the community center or out in my garden, places that used to help, I feel like I’m just going through the motions. I might smile, but it doesn’t really feel real.
Are your feelings of sadness or heaviness present for most of the day, or are they more intermittent?

It’s there most of the day, most days. It’s not like it comes and goes in short bursts. That heaviness just kind of sits with me, even when I’m at the community center or in the garden. I can still do things, but I feel like I’m going through the motions.
Do you feel like you've lost interest or pleasure in social activities, like spending time with friends or family?

Yes. I’ve stepped back from things like gallery events and the walking-club outings I used to always try to go to. I just don’t feel like being around people much, even when I know I probably should. It’s started affecting work too—I’ve been putting off client follow-ups at the credit office.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes. I mean, I can still do the activities, but I don’t really feel much from them. The community center, my garden—those used to lift me up, and now most days there’s just this dull heaviness there. I feel like I’m going through the motions, maybe smiling, but it feels pasted on.
Have there been any periods over the past two years where you felt completely back to normal, without any depressive symptoms?
No, not really. It’s been going on since my close friend died a little over two years ago. I might have a better day here and there, but I haven’t felt completely back to normal.
